title: Residue projection formula transfers the open-image Tor estimate to pro-etale coefficients
statement:
Fix a field $k$, a prime $\ell$ invertible in $k$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$, its valuation ring $R=\mathcal O_E$, a uniformizer $\varpi$, and $A_n=R/\varpi^n$ for $n\ge1$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Let $X$ be separated of finite type over $k$, $i:Z\hookrightarrow X$ a closed immersion and $j:U\hookrightarrow X$ its complementary open immersion [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties]. Use the small pro-etale sites and the coefficient categories $D^b_c(T,A_n)$ and $D^b_c(T,R)$ of [def-weil-derived-complete-integral-detailed], for $T=X,Z,U$.
Fix $n\ge1$ and put $A=A_n$, $\kappa=A/(\varpi)$. Let $N\ge0$ be an integer such that $R^qj_{{\rm et},*}M=0$ for every etale $A$-module sheaf $M$ and $q>N$ [def-weil-pbc-direct-image]. For integers $a\le b$ and $G\in D^b_c(U,A)$ of Tor amplitude $[a,b]$ [def-weil-finite-tor-amplitude], choose any bounded constructible etale origin $G'$ with $\nu_U^*G'\cong G$ [def-weil-pbc-site-comparison-morphism]. The canonical projection morphism is an isomorphism in the etale derived category
$$Rj_{{\rm et},*}G'\otimes_A^L\kappa_X\xrightarrow{\sim}Rj_{{\rm et},*}(G'\otimes_A^L\kappa_U).$$
The right side has cohomology only in $[a,b+N]$. The qcqs direct-image comparison and monoidal comparison pullback identify its pullback with $Rj_*G\otimes_A^L\kappa_X$. Consequently $Rj_*G$ is bounded constructible of Tor amplitude $[a,b+N]$ on the pro-etale site, with the all-module-sheaf meaning of Tor amplitude. All comparisons are the canonical adjunction projection maps, natural in $G$, and independent of the etale origin. The assertion uses a finitely presented residue module, and does not assume $\kappa$ is perfect over $A$. Tensor and the functors are those of [def-weil-derived-tensor, def-weil-derived-direct-image].

source.place: Clause (1 prime) and projection formula for kappa; returned step 17

proof.text: The coefficient ring $A=R/(\varpi^n)$ is finite local by the coefficient-quotient theorem, applied to the DVR $R$ with finite residue field. In particular $A$ is Noetherian: every ideal is generated by its finite set of elements. The exact presentation $A\xrightarrow{\varpi}A\to\kappa\to0$ shows directly that $\kappa$ is finitely presented, including $n=1$, when $\varpi=0$ in $A$. The finite-type Noetherian theorem makes $X$ Noetherian since the spectrum of a field is Noetherian. Every open subscheme of a Noetherian scheme is Noetherian. For an affine open $V\subset X$, therefore $U\cap V$ is quasi-compact, proving $j$ quasi-compact. An open immersion is a monomorphism, so its diagonal is an isomorphism; thus $j$ is separated, hence quasi-separated. These check the qcqs hypotheses below.

source.place: Finite stage and Projection formula for kappa: coefficient and qcqs hypotheses

proof.text: Put $F=G'$. The comparison Tor-interval theorem at $U$ applies because $F$ is bounded below and $A$ is finite. Its reverse implication, applied to $\nu_U^*F\cong G$, gives etale Tor amplitude $[a,b]$ for $F$, with tests against all etale module sheaves. In particular its test against $\kappa_U$ gives $C=F\otimes_A^L\kappa_U\in D^{[a,b]}(U_{\rm et},A)$. This argument never assumes that tensoring an arbitrary bounded complex with $\kappa$ remains bounded.

source.place: (1 prime) at the finite stage: interval for the residue tensor

proof.text: Apply the finitely presented constant-coefficient projection theorem to $f=j$, $K=F$, $M=\kappa$. Its Noetherian, bounded-above and all-module higher-direct-image hypotheses are respectively Step 1, boundedness of $F$, and the assumed bound $N$. It gives exactly the asserted canonical isomorphism $\pi_e:Rj_{{\rm et},*}F\otimes_A^L\kappa_X\xrightarrow{\sim}Rj_{{\rm et},*}C$. The map is the adjunction mate of the pullback tensor comparison followed by counit tensor identity. In particular this invocation uses finite presentation, with no finite-projective-dimension assumption on $\kappa$.

source.place: Projection formula for kappa; finite-free approximation argument is the existing general projection theorem

proof.text: Use the truncation spectral sequence for the additive left exact module direct image $j_*$ (the module categories are Grothendieck abelian). Applied to $C$, its page is $E_2^{p,q}=R^pj_*\mathcal H^q(C)$ and it converges to $\mathcal H^{p+q}(Rj_*C)$ with finite filtration in each total degree. Step 2 forces $a\le q\le b$; the hypothesis forces $0\le p\le N$. Thus every graded piece is zero outside $[a,b+N]$ and so is the finite filtered abutment. In the same spectral sequence for $F$, only finitely many $q$ occur and the same $p$ range applies. Every $E_2$ sheaf is constructible by open-immersion finiteness; kernels, cokernels and finite extensions remain constructible by the constructible Serre theorem. Therefore $H=Rj_{{\rm et},*}F$ is bounded constructible. Step 3 and the etale residue criterion now give etale Tor amplitude $[a,b+N]$ for $H$.

source.place: (1 prime) at the finite stage: truncation spectral sequence and finite-stage constructibility

proof.text:
The canonical qcqs direct-image mate gives $b_F:
u_X^*H\xrightarrow{\sim}Rj_*
u_U^*F$, hence $Rj_*G\cong
u_X^*H$. The finite-ring constructible derived comparison shows that this is bounded intrinsically constructible. Apply the forward implication of the comparison Tor-interval theorem to the bounded-below object $H$ and the interval obtained in Step 4. It gives the Tor amplitude $[a,b+N]$ for $Rj_*G$, explicitly testing every pro-etale module sheaf, including ones without etale origin. This avoids imposing the global finite-field hypothesis of the separate pro-etale residue-test node.

source.place: Hence, after Projection formula for kappa: pro-etale preservation and Tor bound

proof.text:
For completeness the identification of the residue tensors is canonical: use the tensor-pullback isomorphism for $
u_X$, the constant-section-preserving identification $
u_X^*\kappa_X=\kappa_X$, and $b_F$ to identify $
u_X^*(H\otimes_A^L\kappa_X)$ with $Rj_*G\otimes_A^L\kappa_X$. Together with $
u_X^*(\pi_e)$ this identifies the pullback of the right side in Step 3 with that tensor. Exact comparison pullback commutes with cohomology, so it carries the interval in Step 4 to the same interval. To check the actual arrows, apply the etale/pro-etale projection comparison identity with $p=j$, $K=F$, $N=\kappa_X$ and $L=C$. Both $F$ and $C$ are bounded below by Step 2, so both normalized direct-image mates in that identity exist and are isomorphisms. The identity states that the transported $\pi_e$ is exactly the pro-etale adjunction projection map, rather than an unspecified isomorphism.

source.place: Projection formula for kappa: canonical tensor and direct-image comparisons

proof.text: The projection map defined by unit, tensor comparison and counit is natural in $F$: for $u:F\to F_1$, both adjoint transposes become $(u\otimes1)\circ(\varepsilon_F\otimes1)$, by naturality of the counit. The direct-image mate and the tensor comparisons used above are natural in their inputs. Given two origins $(F,e)$ and $(F_1,e_1)$ for $G$, fully faithful bounded-below comparison supplies a unique isomorphism $u:F\to F_1$ with $\nu_U^*u=e_1^{-1}e$. These naturality squares identify all the displayed maps. For three origins the unique lifts compose, proving coherence and independence of origin; the same squares applied to a morphism $G\to G_1$ prove naturality in $G$.

source.place: Projection formula for kappa: naturality and independence of etale origin
